findings.statement: validate_pullback and validate_pushout omit their declared object/leg boundaries. In the lawful terminal category{A,id_A}, set every named morphism to id_A but all declared apex/left/right object fields to Ghost. The square commutes, and every searched Hom involving Ghost is empty, so the universal loop has no candidate cones and returns no violation. A nonexistent object is thus accepted as the proposed pullback/pushout. Canonical ambient-category validation alone cannot repair this missing diagram admission.

check_terminal and check_initial only iterate ambient objects; they never first require the proposed object to belong to the category. In the valid empty category both loops are vacuous and any label passes, although there is no terminal or initial object. This is a missing existence check distinct from the hom-set uniqueness condition.

check_local_confluence accepts a formal-inverse homotopy as a join when the forward branches have no common descendant. For a->b and a->c with b,c irreducible, declare paths r_ab;r_ab^-1 and r_ac;r_ac^-1 and a homotopy between them. Both paths run a->a and pass the structural validator; the checker then reports local confluence and termination despite the two distinct normal forms. This is a chosen zigzag/homotopy condition, not ordinary directed local confluence, and cannot be used with the usual terminating-plus-local-confluence conclusion.

A level2 RewriteCell inserted through add_higher_cell can connect nonparallel paths and still validate. check_two_cell_endpoints only checks that both paths exist; parallel boundary validation occurs only for the separate homotopies map, whose coverage/agreement with cells is not enforced. Paths a->b and c->d with distinct endpoints, joined by such a level2 cell and an empty homotopies map, pass every visible validator stage. The admitted data need not be globular even at level2.

The type therefore cannot serve as an enduring admission token even for the limited reference/shape predicates its constructor checks. Other private validated owners in this audit avoid this specific bypass.

ValidatedFiniteTwoCategory::try_new returns Ok unconditionally, with a placeholder for full validation. A declaration containing object A and no1-identity is accepted; id_1(A) then reaches unreachable because the promised map is absent. No identity, composition, associativity, globularity or interchange admission occurs in this constructor. This is directly visible source behavior; independent branch control is not a Rust run.

lawvere.rs identifies a Lawvere theory as a Cauchy-complete monoid in Prof, but supplies no finite-power/product structure or product-preserving presentation. Idempotent completeness is insufficient: the one-object C2 group category has only the identity idempotent, which splits, yet no terminal object because its sole endomorphism set has two elements. The defining zero-fold product is therefore absent. The implementation should be treated as syntax and selected substitution checks, not that claimed characterization.

findings.statement: classify_cover bounds only the final product of local report counts, then materializes Cartesian prefixes in cover order. A valid presheaf with counts empty:1,A:N,B:0,AunionB:0 has final product0 for cover[A,B], so limit0 passes, yet the first prefix allocates N tuples. Reversing the cover avoids this allocation. The numerical final-product test is correct but does not bound intermediate enumeration work; this is an operational limit gap, not a false sheaf-cover result.

TriangleWitness is described for monotone maps on a finite chain but never checks monotonicity. Taking both left and right maps to be the swap[1,0] gives both composites equal to identity, so both triangle equations and both unit/counit inequalities hold. The maps reverse0<1 and fail the Galois equivalence atx=0,y=0. Thus these predicates alone do not certify an adjunction of chain categories.

AgentFunctor.map_skill_morphism does not preserve the represented SkillMorphism composition: mapping f >> g gives Agent[f >> g], while composing Agent[f] with Agent[g] gives Agent[f] >> Agent[g]. There is no quotient or equality rule identifying those IDs. Separately, SkillMorphism.try_associate compares only four fields even though derived PartialEq includes descriptions, whose two bracketings differ. These are metadata operations with limited field checks, not validated categorical functor/associativity laws on full SkillMorphism values.

IntegerFiniteCategoryWitness admits the reflexive graph with objects0,1,2 and arrows(0,0),(1,1),(2,2),(0,1),(1,2). Every endpoint is in range and every object has a loop, so its complete visible predicate passes. The composable pair0->1->2 has no possible0->2 composite; no category with exactly that arrow inventory exists. Loop existence is not identity or composition certification.

ProductCardinality checks pair-tag syntax and vector length but not unique Cartesian membership. With declared sizes2 and2, four copies of a|x are admitted as four objects even though there is only one distinct pair. The witness therefore establishes a list-size equation, not a complete product-object inventory.

DiscreteCleavageWitness uses only source/target base-object labels when counting lifts, never the projected base arrow. For the valid functor from the terminal category into the one-object group C2, the sole total identity maps to the base identity, so the nonidentity base arrow has no lift. Encoding both base arrows as(0,0) and the sole total arrow as(0,0) passes the source count loop twice. Boundary multiplicity is not cartesian-lift evidence; category and functor admission are also absent.

ValidatedFiniteMonad does not validate its declared category. On the nonassociative three-element unital magma from RCT-P01, the identity endomap and eta=mu=e satisfy its functor, boundary, naturality and monad-equation predicates. The host structure is not a category, so category admission is a necessary missing premise despite the private monad wrapper.

Generic EMAlgebra::verify_laws calls two methods that unconditionally return true; AlgebraMorphism::respects_algebras also returns true without invoking its comparison closure. For Maybe<bool>, the constant-false action violates the unit law at true but is accepted by this visible generic branch. The separate four-shell bool checker uses a different, lawful fixed action and does not justify the generic APIs.

The legacy adjunction validator checks triangle identities without unit/counit naturality. On the valid one-object S3 category with both functors identity, a noncentral transposition as both unit and counit satisfies both triangles but fails naturality against a second transposition. It can also skip triangles when present component names have no functor image. Thus its passing report does not certify an adjunction.

Legacy adjunction validation overwrites cloned embedded functor maps from independent public legacy maps, but DerivedMonad reads the embedded maps and DerivedComonad mixes both representations. Starting from a valid singleton identity adjunction, clearing only embedded left maps leaves the validated legacy data unchanged yet derives an empty monad object/arrow/multiplication map. Its law helpers then return no violations by empty iteration. No immutable validated wrapper connects these steps.

The hom-adjunction validator establishes bijections only for supplied pairs, with no complete pair coverage or naturality. An empty witness vector passes vacuously. Even with the sole pair fully covered, inversion on the C3 hom-set is an exact bijection but fails naturality for identity functors: inverse(0+1)=2 differs from inverse(0)+1=1. Therefore its finite round-trip check is not a full hom-adjunction certificate.

ValidatedFiniteNatTrans does not admit its functor arguments. For a valid singleton category with identity e, two declared identity object maps with empty arrow maps and component e pass all visible natural-transformation checks: the naturality loop skips each missing F(e) or G(e). Neither declaration is a total functor. Independent functor validation would reject both.

ValidatedFiniteOperad::try_new omits associativity. A one-color, three-unary-operation table with unit e, a*a=b and a*b=b*a=b*b=e satisfies every constructor check, yet (a*a)*b=e differs from a*(a*b)=a. This is source-checked admission of a nonassociative structure, not a native Rust replay.

The same constructor checks only declared composition entries and never requires each operation color to belong to colors.
